tip: Καταρχήν (katarkhin) = in principle; καταρχάς (katarkhas) = first of all – even native speakers swap them. Here καταρχήν opens a matter of principle, not a list.
Δεδομένου ότι (dhedhomenou oti) = given that. It is a fixed phrase from older Greek – treat the two words as one chunk meaning 'since'.
Λαμβανομένων υπόψη (lamvanomenon ipopsi = taking into account) changes its ending to match των περιορισμών (ton periorismon = the limits). Everyday Greek normally uses λαμβάνοντας (lamvanontas).
The raised dot after παρακινεί (parakini) is the ano teleia – Greek's semicolon. The ; symbol has a different job in Greek: it is the question mark.
Πρίσμα (prisma) is literally 'prism': υπό αυτό το πρίσμα (ipo afto to prisma = under this prism) is how Greek says 'seen in this light'.
